title: No common zero and permutation invariance
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme and $n\ge1$. Write $\mathbf P^1_S=\mathbf P(\{0,1\};S)=S\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\mathbf P^1_{\mathbf Z}$ and $\mathbf P^n_S=\mathbf P(\{0,\dots,n\};S)=S\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change], with structure morphisms $q_1,q_n$ (the first projections). Let $(\mathbf P^1_S)^n=\mathbf P^1_S\times_S\cdots\times_S\mathbf P^1_S$ be the $n$-fold fibre product over $S$ [def-pc-fibre-product] (formed inductively, $(\mathbf P^1_S)^1=\mathbf P^1_S$, $(\mathbf P^1_S)^m=(\mathbf P^1_S)^{m-1}\times_S\mathbf P^1_S$), with its projections $\mathrm{pr}_i:(\mathbf P^1_S)^n\to\mathbf P^1_S$ ($1\le i\le n$) and $p_n=q_1\circ\mathrm{pr}_i:(\mathbf P^1_S)^n\to S$; a morphism $T\to(\mathbf P^1_S)^n$ is the same as an $n$-tuple of morphisms $a_i:T\to\mathbf P^1_S$ with $q_1\circ a_1=\dots=q_1\circ a_n$.

*The sections.* Let $\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^1_{\mathbf Z}}(1)$ be the twisting sheaf of $\mathbf P^1_{\mathbf Z}=\operatorname{Proj}\mathbf Z[T_0,T_1]$ [def-pc-projective-space-twist] (with $A=\mathbf Z$, $n=1$), with its global sections $T_0,T_1$ (on $D_+(T_k)$, $T_l=(T_l/T_k)\,e_k^{(1)}$), let $\mathcal O(1)$ on $\mathbf P^1_S$ be its pullback along the second projection $\mathbf P^1_S\to\mathbf P^1_{\mathbf Z}$, with the pulled-back sections $T_0,T_1$, and put

$$
\mathcal L_n=\mathrm{pr}_1^*\mathcal O(1)\otimes\cdots\otimes\mathrm{pr}_n^*\mathcal O(1),\qquad x_i=\mathrm{pr}_i^*T_0,\ \ y_i=\mathrm{pr}_i^*T_1\in\Gamma\bigl((\mathbf P^1_S)^n,\mathrm{pr}_i^*\mathcal O(1)\bigr),
$$

an invertible $\mathcal O_{(\mathbf P^1_S)^n}$-module [def-sc-invertible-module] (the line bundle $\mathcal O(1,\dots,1)$). Let $F_0,\dots,F_n\in\mathbf Z[x_1,y_1,\dots,x_n,y_n]$ be the polynomials of [def-weil-pbc-symmetric-product-morphism], $\prod_{i=1}^n(x_it+y_i)=\sum_{j=0}^nF_jt^j$. Then:

(a) $F_j=\sum_{J\subseteq\{1,\dots,n\},\,|J|=j}m_J$ with $m_J=\prod_{i\in J}x_i\prod_{i\notin J}y_i$; so $F_j$ is multihomogeneous of degree $(1,\dots,1)$ in the pairs $(x_i,y_i)$, and we also write $F_j$ for the global section $\sum_{|J|=j}u_{J,1}\otimes\cdots\otimes u_{J,n}$ of $\mathcal L_n$, where $u_{J,i}=x_i$ for $i\in J$ and $u_{J,i}=y_i$ for $i\notin J$.

(b) (*no common zero*) For every point $z$ of $(\mathbf P^1_S)^n$ some $F_j(z)\ne0$ in the fibre $\mathcal L_n(z)=\mathcal L_{n,z}\otimes\kappa(z)$; that is, $F_0,\dots,F_n$ generate $\mathcal L_n$ in the sense of [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-functor-of-points].

(c) Hence the *symmetric-product morphism*

$$
\sigma_n:=\varphi_{p_n,(\mathcal L_n,(F_0,\dots,F_n))}:(\mathbf P^1_S)^n\longrightarrow\mathbf P^n_S
$$

of [def-weil-pbc-morphism-to-projective-space-by-sections] is defined: $\mathrm{pr}_1\circ\sigma_n=p_n$ and $\mathrm{pr}_2\circ\sigma_n=\psi_{(\mathcal L_n,(F_j))}:(\mathbf P^1_S)^n\to\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}$, the morphism with $\psi^*\mathcal O(1)\cong\mathcal L_n$, $\psi^*T_j\mapsto F_j$; on coordinates it is $((x_1:y_1),\dots,(x_n:y_n))\mapsto[F_0:\cdots:F_n]$.

(d) (*$S_n$-invariance*) For a permutation $\pi$ of $\{1,\dots,n\}$ let $\tau_\pi:(\mathbf P^1_S)^n\to(\mathbf P^1_S)^n$ be the morphism with $\mathrm{pr}_i\circ\tau_\pi=\mathrm{pr}_{\pi(i)}$ for all $i$ (an automorphism over $S$, with inverse $\tau_{\pi^{-1}}$). Then there is an isomorphism $\beta_\pi:\tau_\pi^*\mathcal L_n\to\mathcal L_n$ with $\beta_\pi(\tau_\pi^*F_j)=F_j$ for all $j$ (the $F_j$ are $S_n$-invariant), and $\sigma_n\circ\tau_\pi=\sigma_n$.

proof.text: *The $F_j$ and their sections.* Apply [lem-weil-pbc-product-linear-forms-coefficients] with $R=\mathbf Z[x_1,y_1,\dots,x_n,y_n]$, $a_i=x_i$, $b_i=y_i$: the coefficient $F_j$ of $t^j$ in $\prod_i(x_it+y_i)$ is $\sum_{|J|=j}m_J$, $m_J=\prod_{i\in J}x_i\prod_{i\notin J}y_i$. Each $m_J$ contains, for every $i$, exactly one of $x_i,y_i$, to the first power; so $F_j$ is multihomogeneous of degree $(1,\dots,1)$, and replacing the commutative product $m_J$ by the tensor product $u_{J,1}\otimes\cdots\otimes u_{J,n}$ of the sections $u_{J,i}\in\{x_i,y_i\}\subset\Gamma(\mathrm{pr}_i^*\mathcal O(1))$ (in the order $i=1,\dots,n$ of the factors of $\mathcal L_n$) gives a well-defined global section $F_j$ of $\mathcal L_n$. $\mathcal L_n$ is invertible as a tensor product of pullbacks of the invertible module $\mathcal O(1)$ [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor](1); $\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^1_{\mathbf Z}}(1)$ is invertible by its construction [def-pc-projective-space-twist].

source.place: Etale Cohomology, proof of Lemma 0A4F: the F_j are the integer polynomials with prod(x_i t + y_i) = sum F_j t^{n-j} (Stacks indexes in reverse order)

proof.text: *$T_0,T_1$ have no common zero on $\mathbf P^1_S$.* A point $w$ of $\mathbf P^1_{\mathbf Z}=\operatorname{Proj}\mathbf Z[T_0,T_1]$ is a homogeneous prime not containing the irrelevant ideal $(T_0,T_1)$, so it lies in $D_+(T_0)$ or in $D_+(T_1)$ (Stacks 01NG). On $D_+(T_k)$ the section $T_k$ of $\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^1_{\mathbf Z}}(1)$ is the basis $e_k^{(1)}$ [def-pc-projective-space-twist], so $T_k(w)\ne0$ in the fibre $\mathcal O(1)(w)$. For a point $v$ of $\mathbf P^1_S$ with image $w$ in $\mathbf P^1_{\mathbf Z}$, the fibre of the pullback is $\mathcal O(1)(v)=\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^1_{\mathbf Z}}(1)(w)\otimes_{\kappa(w)}\kappa(v)$ with $T_k(v)=T_k(w)\otimes1$ [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor](3), which is nonzero since a nonzero vector stays nonzero under a field extension. Hence for every $v$, $(T_0(v),T_1(v))\ne(0,0)$.

source.place: ## Proof: 'A common zero of all F_j would make the product the zero polynomial in t, forcing some pair (x_i,y_i) to vanish, which is impossible in P^1'

proof.text: *The morphism $\sigma_n$ (part (c)).* By steps 1 and 3, $(\mathcal L_n,(F_0,\dots,F_n))$ is an invertible module with generating global sections on $(\mathbf P^1_S)^n$, and $p_n:(\mathbf P^1_S)^n\to S$ is a morphism. So [def-weil-pbc-morphism-to-projective-space-by-sections] gives $\sigma_n=\varphi_{p_n,(\mathcal L_n,(F_j))}$, the unique morphism into $\mathbf P^n_S=S\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}$ with $\mathrm{pr}_1\circ\sigma_n=p_n$ and $\mathrm{pr}_2\circ\sigma_n=\psi_{(\mathcal L_n,(F_j))}$, the morphism of [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-functor-of-points] (Stacks 01NE) with $\psi^*\mathcal O(1)\cong\mathcal L_n$ carrying $\psi^*T_j$ to $F_j$; this is the formula $((x_i:y_i))_i\mapsto[F_0:\cdots:F_n]$ of [def-weil-pbc-symmetric-product-morphism].

proof.text: *The permutation automorphisms and invariance of the $F_j$.* By the universal property of the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product], applied inductively, a morphism into $(\mathbf P^1_S)^n$ is an $n$-tuple of morphisms into $\mathbf P^1_S$ with the same composite to $S$; so $\tau_\pi:=(\mathrm{pr}_{\pi(1)},\dots,\mathrm{pr}_{\pi(n)})$ is the unique morphism with $\mathrm{pr}_i\circ\tau_\pi=\mathrm{pr}_{\pi(i)}$; $p_n\circ\tau_\pi=q_1\circ\mathrm{pr}_{\pi(1)}=p_n$, and $\tau_\pi\circ\tau_{\pi^{-1}}$, $\tau_{\pi^{-1}}\circ\tau_\pi$ have the same projections as the identity, so they are the identity. By [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor](2), $\tau_\pi^*\mathrm{pr}_i^*\mathcal O(1)\cong(\mathrm{pr}_i\circ\tau_\pi)^*\mathcal O(1)=\mathrm{pr}_{\pi(i)}^*\mathcal O(1)$ with $\tau_\pi^*x_i\mapsto x_{\pi(i)}$, $\tau_\pi^*y_i\mapsto y_{\pi(i)}$, and $\tau_\pi^*\mathcal L_n\cong\bigotimes_i\mathrm{pr}_{\pi(i)}^*\mathcal O(1)$; composing with the symmetry isomorphism that moves the $i$-th factor to position $\pi(i)$ gives $\beta_\pi:\tau_\pi^*\mathcal L_n\to\mathcal L_n$ with $\beta_\pi(\tau_\pi^*(u_{J,1}\otimes\cdots\otimes u_{J,n}))=u_{\pi(J),1}\otimes\cdots\otimes u_{\pi(J),n}$ (the factor $u_{J,i}$, which is $x_i$ or $y_i$ according as $i\in J$, becomes $x_{\pi(i)}$ or $y_{\pi(i)}$, i.e. the factor $u_{\pi(J),\pi(i)}$). Since $J\mapsto\pi(J)$ is a bijection of the $j$-element subsets of $\{1,\dots,n\}$, the formula of step 1 gives $\beta_\pi(\tau_\pi^*F_j)=F_j$. (On polynomials: permuting the pairs $(x_i,y_i)$ permutes the factors of $\prod_i(x_it+y_i)$, so it fixes every coefficient $F_j$.)

source.place: ## Proof: 'Permuting the factors fixes every F_j'

proof.text: *$\sigma_n\circ\tau_\pi=\sigma_n$ (part (d)).* Both are morphisms into the fibre product $\mathbf P^n_S=S\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}$, so by [def-pc-fibre-product] it suffices to compare the two projections. First, $\mathrm{pr}_1\circ\sigma_n\circ\tau_\pi=p_n\circ\tau_\pi=p_n=\mathrm{pr}_1\circ\sigma_n$ (step 5). Second, $\mathrm{pr}_2\circ\sigma_n\circ\tau_\pi=\psi_{(\mathcal L_n,(F_j))}\circ\tau_\pi=\psi_{(\tau_\pi^*\mathcal L_n,(\tau_\pi^*F_j))}$ by the compatibility with pullback in [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-functor-of-points], and the pair $(\tau_\pi^*\mathcal L_n,(\tau_\pi^*F_j))$ is equivalent to $(\mathcal L_n,(F_j))$ via $\beta_\pi$ (step 5), so by the same node this is $\psi_{(\mathcal L_n,(F_j))}=\mathrm{pr}_2\circ\sigma_n$. Hence $\sigma_n\circ\tau_\pi=\sigma_n$ [def-weil-pbc-morphism-to-projective-space-by-sections].

split_report.summary: Made the statement precise without changing sigma_n: it is now explicitly the morphism phi_{p_n,(L_n,(F_j))} of def-weil-pbc-morphism-to-projective-space-by-sections (created by the over-base worker; same name, same formula, same L_n = pr_1^*O(1) (x) ... (x) pr_n^*O(1), x_i = pr_i^*T_0, y_i = pr_i^*T_1 as in lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-product-over-base), with O(1) on P^1_S the pullback of the twisting sheaf of P^1_Z (def-pc-projective-space-twist). Stated (a) the coefficient formula F_j = sum_{|J|=j} prod_J x_i prod_{J^c} y_i and the meaning of F_j as a section of L_n; (b) no common zero as fibrewise non-vanishing (the generation condition of lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-functor-of-points); (c) the definition of sigma_n; (d) S_n-invariance as sigma_n o tau_pi = sigma_n for the permutation automorphisms tau_pi (pr_i o tau_pi = pr_{pi(i)}), together with the invariance beta_pi(tau_pi^*F_j) = F_j. The one imported step (elementary null, no uses) is split into six steps: coefficients and sections, T_0,T_1 without common zero on P^1 (Stacks 01NG), the fibre computation with kappa[t] a domain, the morphism (Stacks 01NE/01NF), the permutation isomorphism beta_pi, and the comparison of the two projections. New nodes: lem-weil-pbc-product-linear-forms-coefficients (Mathlib leaf, Finset.prod_add) and lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor (unsplit; pullback/tensor/fibres of invertible modules, Stacks 01CD, 0B8L, 0B8K, 0098, 01CB). stmt_deps: added the projective-space, fibre-product, twisting-sheaf, invertible-module, functor-of-points and phi nodes; def-weil-pbc-symmetric-product-morphism kept.
